what: A virtual species and a clustered survey
title: Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes
text: Twelve autocorrelated predictor layers; species responds first three. draw single clustered survey training data, fit model K = 5 covariates (three real ones plus two noise). held-evaluation set built way pseudo-absence test sets usually : enriched, every held-presence plus three times many absences. prevalence (~0.25) far landscape’s, one gap lsed corrects .
code: nx <- ny <- 80; P <- 12; K <- 5 r0 <- rast(nrows = ny, ncols = nx, xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = 0, ymax = 1) xy <- xyFromCell(r0, 1:ncell(r0))  smooth_field <- function(x, y, nh = 4, mf = 1.6) {   # one autocorrelated layer   v <- numeric(length(x))   for (k in 1:nh)     v <- v + rnorm(1) * sin(2 * pi * (runif(1, -mf, mf) * x +                                       runif(1, -mf, mf) * y) + runif(1, 0, 2 * pi))   as.numeric(scale(v)) } L   <- sapply(1:P, function(j) smooth_field(xy[, 1], xy[, 2])) env <- rast(r0, nlyr = P); values(env) <- L; names(env) <- sprintf("v%02d", 1:P)  # true niche: depends on v01-v03 only pres    <- rbinom(nrow(L), 1,                   plogis(-3.0 + 1.8 * L[, 1] - 1.4 * L[, 2] + 1.0 * L[, 3]                          - 0.7 * L[, 1] * L[, 2])) pi_land <- mean(pres) # TRUE landscape prevalence vars    <- names(env)[1:K]  # one clustered survey -> training data n_tr <- 500; rad <- 0.22 sx <- pmin(pmax(0.5 + rnorm(n_tr, 0, rad), 0), 1) sy <- pmin(pmax(0.5 + rnorm(n_tr, 0, rad), 0), 1) tr_cells <- cellFromXY(env, cbind(sx, sy)) train <- as.data.frame(L[tr_cells, 1:K]); names(train) <- vars train$pa <- factor(ifelse(pres[tr_cells] == 1, "pres", "abs"),                    levels = c("abs", "pres")) # caret wants a factor outcome  round(pi_land, 3) #> [1] 0.149 pool <- setdiff(1:ncell(env), tr_cells) pp   <- pool[pres[pool] == 1] pa   <- pool[pres[pool] == 0] ev_cells <- c(pp, sample(pa, 3 * length(pp))) # ~1:3 presence:absence eval <- as.data.frame(L[ev_cells, 1:K]); names(eval) <- vars y    <- pres[ev_cells] round(mean(y), 3) # enriched design prevalence #> [1] 0.25

what: Fit a GLM using Caret and its area of applicability
title: Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes
text: Scoring inside area applicability keeps comparison honest. model judged performs interpolating portions landscape user cares detecting new occurrences , training data model.
code: m <- train(x = train[vars], y = train$pa,            method = "glm", family = "binomial",            trControl = trainControl(method = "none", classProbs = TRUE))  prob <- predict(m, eval, type = "prob")[, "pres"] # held-out predictions  # AOA from CAST, weighted by the fitted model's variable importance aoa_r <- aoa(newdata = env[[vars]], model = m, verbose = FALSE) di    <- terra::extract(aoa_r$DI, xy[ev_cells, ])[, 1] in_aoa <- di <= aoa_r$parameters$threshold # keep interpolation points only truth <- y[in_aoa] pred  <- prob[in_aoa] pi0   <- mean(truth) # in-AOA (design) prevalence

what: Route 1 — summary: from one reported number to a decision curve
title: Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes
text: Suppose carried away PR-AUC prevalence measured . ap_scalar_to_prev() recovers equal-variance binormal ROC reproduces , re-prices precision landscape prevalence; nb_binormal() reads best-achievable net benefit ROC, nb_binormal_band() turns assumed spread PR-AUC plausibility band.
code: pr_auc <- ap_pointwise(truth, pred, pi0) pt     <- seq(0.001, 0.25, by = 0.002) # threshold probabilities  rec <- ap_scalar_to_prev(pr_auc, pi0 = pi0, pi_target = pi_land) rec[c("mu", "implied_roc_auc", "ap_target")] #> $mu #> [1] 2.242677 #>  #> $implied_roc_auc #> [1] 0.9436091 #>  #> $ap_target #> [1] 0.801286  nb_sum   <- nb_binormal(rec$mu, pi_land, pt) band_sum <- nb_binormal_band(pr_auc, pi_land, pt, spread = 0.04, pi0 = pi0)

what: Route 2 — per-point: the decision curve from the raw data
title: Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes
text: predictions hand can calculate decision-curve analysis directly. First check calibration; predictions produced enriched sample, shift landscape prevalence recalibrate_to_prevalence() thresholding. nb_exact() net benefit surveying every unit threshold, nb_exact_ci() bootstrap band, nb_treat_all() survey-everything reference.
code: cox_calibration(truth, pred) # intercept, slope #> cox_intercept     cox_slope  #>     0.4558527     1.0647456  pred_rc <- recalibrate_to_prevalence(pred, pi0, pi_land)  nb_pt <- nb_exact(truth, pred_rc, pi_land, pt) ci_pt <- nb_exact_ci(truth, pred_rc, pi_land, pt, B = 499, level = 0.8) nb_all <- nb_treat_all(pi_land, pt) # treat-none is identically 0

Either way evaluation anchored landscape prevalence, test set’s. Grimmett, L., Whitsed, R., & Horta, . (2021). Presence-species distribution models sensitive sample prevalence: Evaluating models using spatial prediction stability accuracy metrics. Ecography, 44(9).
code: df <- rbind(   data.frame(     pt = pt, nb = nb_pt,  lo = ci_pt$lower,        strat = "SDM — per-point (raw data)"),   data.frame(     pt = pt, nb = nb_sum, lo = band_sum$lower,      strat = "SDM — summary (reported PR-AUC)"),   data.frame(     pt = pt, nb = nb_all, lo = NA,     strat = "Survey all"),   data.frame(     pt = pt, nb = 0, lo = NA,     strat = "Survey none") )  ggplot(df, aes(pt, nb, colour = strat)) +   geom_ribbon(data = subset(df, !is.na(lo)),               aes(ymin = lo, ymax = nb, fill = strat),               colour = NA, alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +   coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.02, pi_land * 1.1)) +   scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +   labs(     x = expression(Threshold ~ probability ~ p[t]),      y = "Net benefit",     colour = NULL,     title = sprintf(       "Two routes to the decision curve at %.0f%% landscape prevalence",       100 * pi_land       )     ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(legend.position = "top")
